issues.title: Test file separated from component
issues.description: The rule requires that for every React component file component.tsx, the test file component.test.tsx exists in the same directory. However, the test file schema-form-input-array-list.test.tsx was placed in a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with schema-form-input-array-list.tsx.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: Drag-and-drop reordering swaps source and target indices
issues.description: The handleDragEnd function passes arguments to moveItem in the wrong order - it calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex) instead of moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). This causes drag-and-drop operations to place items in the opposite position from where they're dropped. For example, dragging an item from index 2 to index 0 will incorrectly move the item at index 0 to index 2 instead, creating confusing and incorrect reordering behavior for users.

issues.title: Prefix items incorrectly included in sortable context
issues.description: The sortableKeys array is constructed from all localKeyedValues instead of excluding prefix items. The code removed the .slice(prefixItemsCount) operation, meaning prefix items (which should have fixed positions and not be draggable) are now included in the SortableContext. This allows prefix items to be moved via drag-and-drop, violating the constraint that prefix items must remain in their fixed positions and breaking the schema's structural requirements.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Get the keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)
const sortableKeys = localKeyedValues.map((item) => item.key);

issues.title: Unused local variable `prefixItemsCount` added
issues.description: `prefixItemsCount` is introduced but never referenced anywhere in the component. This leaves unused code in the codebase, violating the rule requiring unused items to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20223 - Add drag-and-drop reordering for schema form arrays
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds drag-and-drop reordering to array items in the ui-v2 schema form using @dnd-kit. A GripVertical handle appears on each non-prefix item, a DndContext/SortableContext wraps the list in SchemaFormInputArrayList, and each SchemaFormInputArrayItem registers a useSortable with disabled: !canMove so tuple (prefixItems) entries stay fixed. Keyboard reordering goes through KeyboardSensor with sortableKeyboardCoordinates, and the existing Move up/Move down menu entries are kept. The dependency additions are consistent with the lockfile and the @dnd-kit peer ranges.

The wiring is reasonable, but the drop handler has a correctness bug. handleDragEnd calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex), and moveItem takes (from, to), so every drag moves the wrong item to the wrong place. The PR also claims behavioral tests for move up/down and prefix immutability, but the diff only adds four snapshot tests, none of which exercise a drag or move. That gap is why the inverted call got through. There is also an unused variable that breaks the TypeScript and Biome checks.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The core feature is broken: handleDragEnd passes the indices to moveItem in reverse, so a drag produces the wrong order (for example, dragging A onto C in [A,B,C] yields [C,A,B] instead of [B,C,A]). The unused prefixItemsCount also fails the project's noUnusedLocals and Biome noUnusedVariables rules. The advertised behavioral tests are absent, so nothing in the suite would catch either problem. Fix these before merge.

architecture.overview:
Array fields in the schema form render through SchemaFormInputArray, which delegates to SchemaFormInputArrayList. That component owns the item list as local keyed state (uuid keys) and pushes changes up through onValuesChange. Before this PR, each row was rendered by SchemaFormInputArrayItem with a per-row dropdown offering Delete, Move up, and Move down. The dropdown is still there. The PR adds a @dnd-kit DndContext and SortableContext around the list, so each row now also acts as a sortable. The sortable's drag handle is rendered only for rows where canMove is true, which excludes prefixItems (tuple) positions.

The new flow has two entry points that both end in the same moveItem helper: pointer or keyboard drags finish in DndContext's onDragEnd, which calls handleDragEnd and then moveItem, and the menu's Move up and Move down call moveItem directly. moveItem splices localKeyedValues and calls onValuesChange. The drag path reverses the index arguments, so only the menu path produces correct ordering today.
steps: Entry point: SchemaFormInputArray renders SchemaFormInputArrayList with the property schema, values, and onValuesChange.

List state: SchemaFormInputArrayList keeps localKeyedValues with stable uuid keys and computes canMove per index from prefixItems. The PR adds sensors (PointerSensor and KeyboardSensor with sortableKeyboardCoordinates), wraps the rows in DndContext and SortableContext, and passes itemKey to each row.

Row: SchemaFormInputArrayItem calls useSortable({ id: itemKey, disabled: !canMove }), applies the transform and opacity, and renders the GripVertical handle (or a spacer for prefix rows). The existing SchemaFormPropertyMenu with Move up and Move down is unchanged.
Drop: handleDragEnd maps active.id and over.id to indices and should call moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). The PR calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex) instead, which is the critical bug.
Tests: the added schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx cases only snapshot the DOM. They cover handle presence and absence but not the reorder logic or the menu actions.

findings.title: Drag-and-drop moves the wrong item because moveItem arguments are reversed
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, `handleDragEnd` (around lines 130-145) calls `moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex)`, but `moveItem(from, to)` (lines 117-122) takes the source index first. Swap the arguments so it calls `moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex)`, which moves the dragged item to the drop target's index. Add a test that renders an array with three string values and fires a dnd-kit drag end (or exercises handleDragEnd through DndContext) to assert the resulting order. Keep the existing `moveUp`/`moveDown` callers untouched.

findings.title: Unused `prefixItemsCount` breaks the TypeScript and Biome checks
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, delete the unused `prefixItemsCount` constant (around lines 45-47). Nothing else references it; prefix detection already lives in `getCanMoveForIndex` and `getPropertyForIndex`. Then confirm the file still passes the TypeScript build (`noUnusedLocals`) and Biome's `noUnusedVariables` rule.

findings.title: Tests claimed in the PR description are missing; only DOM snapshots were added
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx` (the `describe("array")` block around lines 489-565), add behavioral tests alongside the snapshots. Cover: (1) opening the row menu and clicking Move up and Move down, asserting the values passed to `onValuesChange`; (2) the Move up and Move down entries are absent for the first and last items and for prefix items; (3) a drag-end reorder through the DndContext, asserting the new order (this would catch the inverted `moveItem` call in `handleDragEnd`). Use `@testing-library/user-event` and assert outcomes, not internal calls.

findings.title: Misleading comment and prefix keys left in the SortableContext item list
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx`, the comment and `sortableKeys` (around lines 147-148) say only non-prefix items are sortable, but `localKeyedValues.map` includes prefix rows. Build `sortableKeys` from only the rows where `getCanMoveForIndex(index)` is true, and in `handleDragEnd` (around lines 130-145) return early if either the active or the over index fails `getCanMoveForIndex`. Keep the comment accurate to the code.

findings.title: Drag handle removes the focus indicator for keyboard users
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-item.tsx`, the drag handle button (around lines 84-92) uses `focus:outline-none` with no replacement, so keyboard focus is invisible. Replace it with the focus-visible ring pattern used elsewhere in ui-v2 (for example `focus-visible:ring-1 focus-visible:ring-ring` as in the Button and dropdown trigger classes). Keep the dark-mode token and hover classes as they are.

findings.title: Drag handle lacks touch-action, so touch drags will scroll the page
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-item.tsx`, add the `touch-none` Tailwind class to the drag handle button (around lines 84-92) so that dnd-kit's PointerSensor can start drags on touch devices instead of the browser scrolling. Don't change the other classes on the button.

findings.title: New snapshots bake in dnd-kit's global counter ids
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx`, the new array snapshot tests (around lines 489-565) depend on dnd-kit's global counter (`DndDescribedBy-N`, `DndLiveRegion-N`) as well as React `useId`. Either mock `@dnd-kit/core`'s id generation for these tests, or move the drag-handle assertions into behavioral tests that query by role and label (`getByRole('button', { name: 'Drag to reorder' })`) so they don't depend on the order of the snapshots.

findings.title: Prefix items stay fixed in the UI and are excluded from dragging
findings.body:
Prefix (tuple) rows get `useSortable({ disabled: !canMove })` and render a spacer `<div className="w-5" />` in place of the handle, so they can't be picked up. The menu's Move up and Move down entries also stay gated by `canMove`. The snapshot covering prefixItems checks the handle markup on the prefix rows.

This keeps tuple positions stable, which is the requirement that matters most for a fixed-position schema.

findings.title: Stable item keys make the sortable identity reliable
findings.body: Rows are keyed by uuid in `localKeyedValues` and passed to `useSortable` as `itemKey`. The sortable id therefore stays with the row across reorders, edits, and deletes, instead of following the index. The sensors use `sortableKeyboardCoordinates`, so keyboard reordering works with the same logic.
